# Analyze the relationship between introduction pathways and mrt in invasion_success dataset
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Check the distribution of mrt across different introduction pathways
sns.boxplot(x='intro.pathway', y='mrt', data=invasion_success)
plt.title('Distribution of Minimum Residence Time (mrt) by Introduction Pathway')
plt.xlabel('Introduction Pathway')
plt.ylabel('Minimum Residence Time (mrt)')
plt.show()

# Check for statistical significance using ANOVA
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
filtered_data = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group data by 'intro.pathway' and extract mrt values
groups = filtered_data.groupby('intro.pathway')['mrt'].apply(list)

# Perform ANOVA
f_statistic, p_value = f_oneway(*groups)
f_statistic, p_value

# Analyze the relationship between mrt, introduction pathways, and invasion success
# Using 'number.of.invaded.plots' as a measure of invasion success

# Create a scatter plot with mrt on the x-axis and number.of.invaded.plots on the y-axis, colored by introduction pathway
sns.scatterplot(x='mrt', y='number.of.invaded.plots', hue='intro.pathway', data=invasion_success)
plt.title('Invasion Success (Number of Invaded Plots) vs. Minimum Residence Time (mrt) by Introduction Pathway')
plt.xlabel('Minimum Residence Time (mrt)')
plt.ylabel('Number of Invaded Plots')
plt.legend(title='Introduction Pathway')
plt.show()

# Perform a multiple regression analysis to assess the interaction between mrt and introduction pathway on invasion success
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Prepare the data for regression
X = invasion_success[['mrt', 'intro.pathway']]
X = pd.get_dummies(X, drop_first=True)  # One-hot encode the categorical variable 'intro.pathway'
X = sm.add_constant(X)  # Add a constant term for the intercept
y = invasion_success['number.of.invaded.plots']

# Fit the regression model
model = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()

# Display the regression results
model.summary()

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Prepare the data for regression
X = invasion_success[['mrt', 'intro.pathway']]
X = pd.get_dummies(X, drop_first=True)  # One-hot encode the categorical variable 'intro.pathway'
X = np.array(X)  # Convert to numpy array for sklearn
y = np.array(invasion_success['number.of.invaded.plots'])

# Create and fit the regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Display the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
intercept = model.intercept_
coefficients, intercept
